newsitem.title: USA: Clinton lawyer blasts Whitewater prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: Clinton lawyer blasts Whitewater prosecutor.

text.p: An attorney for President Clinton Tuesday accused Whitewater independent counsel Kenneth Starr of flouting legal ethics by trying Clinton and his wife Hillary in the news media.

In a blistering six-page letter, lawyer David Kendall cited a number of legal principles that he said were violated by Starr and his associates in cooperating with the author of an article that appeared this week in the Sunday New York Times Magazine.
"The course you have chosen is unprecedented and profoundly ill-advised for a number of different but mutually reinforcing reasons," Kendall said in a letter to Starr.

Citing the "truly awesome might" given to an independent counsel, Kendall said Starr had a responsibility "to conduct grand jury investigations fairly so that the reputations of those investigated but not charged will not be besmirched."

Kendall charged that the article contained "violations of grand jury secrecy, noting references to closed door legal procedings by the jury into the billing records of Mrs. Clinton when she was an attorney in Arkansas.

"Grand jury secrecy rules are aimed at preventing precisely this kind of lead-and-smear damage," Kendall said. He urged Starr to "abandon your public relations offensive, get on with your investigation in the manner of previous independent counsels, and bring it to a speedy conclusion."
